New single stock ETFs begin trading the day after Anthropic’s U.S. IPO

TORONTO--(BUSINESS WIRE)--Cboe Canada Inc. (“Cboe Canada”) today welcomed Purpose Investments for the launch of two new yield-focused single-stock ETFs, providing exposure to two of the most closely watched names in technology, along with enhanced monthly income. The new funds are now trading under the following names and tickers:

  • Purpose Anthropic (ANT) Yield Shares ETF - ANTY
  • Purpose Micron (MU) Yield Shares ETF – MUY

The Purpose Yield Shares ETFs are designed to provide monthly income while maintaining exposure to most of the long-term potential growth of leading U.S. companies, using covered call strategies and moderate leverage. The ETFs also reduce foreign exchange risk by hedging U.S. exposure back to the Canadian dollar.

The Purpose Anthropic Yield Shares ETF begins trading the day after Anthropic’s U.S. IPO (NASDAQ: ANT), giving Canadian investors an income-generating way to participate in the company as it enters the public market.

“Anthropic and Micron sit at the center of the AI era: one building the models, the other supplying the memory that powers them," said Vlad Tasevski, Chief Innovation Officer at Purpose Investments. "Fast-growing companies like these rarely pay a dividend, so income investors have had to watch them from the sidelines. Yield Shares change that. Canadians can now own the names they believe in and earn a monthly income from them, while maintaining exposure to most of their long-term returns."

“We’re pleased to welcome Purpose back to Cboe Canada with two new additions to the Yield Shares lineup, timed to coincide with one of the year’s most anticipated public debuts,” said Joacim Wiklander, CEO of Cboe Canada. “Purpose continues to bring creative, investor-focused ideas to market, and we’re proud to be their listing venue for the Yield Shares suite.”

The new Yield Shares ETFs are now trading alongside 33 other Purpose ETFs already listed on Cboe Canada. Investors can trade units of all Purpose ETFs through their usual investment channels, including discount brokerage platforms and full-service dealers. For a complete view of all Cboe-listed securities, visit the Cboe Canada listing directory.

Cboe Canada continues to attract innovative ETF and public company issuers by offering a streamlined listing process, competitive fee structure, and access to a diverse and engaged investor base. The exchange is home to ETFs from Canada’s most reputable asset managers, leading Canadian and international growth companies, and an expansive suite of Canadian Depositary Receipts (CDRs). Cboe Canada consistently facilitates close to 15% of all trading volume in Canadian listed securities.

Cboe Canada is Canada’s senior stock exchange providing a best-in-class listing experience for issuers that are shaping the economies of tomorrow. Fully operational since 2015, Cboe Canada lists companies and investment products seeking a robust and internationally recognized platform that enables investor trust, quality liquidity, and broad awareness including unfettered access to market data.

Cboe also powers ETF Market Canada, a user-friendly platform providing investors and advisors with one-stop access to ETF research and analysis. Real-time, institutional-grade data allows users to compare, contrast, and explore the entire universe of 2,000+ Canadian ETFs, free of charge.

This accolade reflects the strength of our culture, the passion and dedication of our employees, and our continued focus on innovation in service to clients. By investing in our people and creating opportunities for growth and engagement, we're building an environment where employees contribute meaningful work and make a lasting impact.”

Developed by Forbes and Statista, the ranking evaluates multinational organizations with at least 1,000 employees. More than 300,000 employees were surveyed anonymously over the past three years and asked about their willingness to recommend their employer, other employers in their industry and organizations within their social circles.

Eligible companies were assessed based on direct evaluations from employees and indirect evaluations from respondents familiar with employers in their industry or through friends, family members, and acquaintances. The final ranking reflects the period from January 2026 to May 2026. Ameriprise did not pay a fee to be evaluated but did pay a fee to publicly cite the results.

Newsweek partnered with Plant-A Insights Group to recognize America’s Greatest Workplaces, chosen based on an independent survey of roughly 179,000 employees. Eligible companies (U.S. companies employing over 1,000 individuals) were evaluated from April to October 2025, across several categories, including corporate culture; work-life-balance; company image; working environment; belonging and community; sustainability & awareness; compensation & benefits; training & career progression; mental wellbeing; job security.   • 48% confirmed overall response rate (ORR) with a 10.4-month median duration of response in the primary analysis population of 65 patients with platinum-resistant/refractory ovarian cancer 

  • 36% ORR with an 8.1-month median duration of response across all cohorts in the overall population of 168 evaluable patients

  • Data presented today as a late-breaking oral presentation at ENA 2026

  • Rezatapopt NDA submission for platinum-resistant/refractory ovarian cancer planned in first quarter of 2027

PRINCETON, N.J., Nov. 20, 2026 (GLOBE NEWSWIRE) -- PMV Pharmaceuticals, Inc. (“PMV Pharma” or the “Company”; Nasdaq: PMVP), a precision oncology company pioneering the discovery and development of small molecule therapies targeting p53, today reported updated results from the pivotal Phase 2 portion of the PYNNACLE clinical trial of rezatapopt monotherapy in patients with TP53 Y220C-mutated advanced solid tumors.

The data presented include investigator-assessed efficacy across all tumor types, including the primary analysis population of 65 platinum-resistant/refractory ovarian cancer patients who received prior standard of care. In this group, the overall response rate (ORR) was 48%, with a median duration of response of 10.4 months. In the overall population across all cohorts among 168 evaluable patients, the ORR was 36% and the median duration of response was 8.1 months.

Results were presented today in a late breaking oral presentation by Alison M. Schram, M.D., Medical Oncologist at Memorial Sloan Kettering Cancer Center and PYNNACLE Study Investigator at the 38th EORTC-NCI-AACR Symposium on Molecular Targets and Cancer Therapeutics (ENA 2026) in Barcelona, Spain.

“Patients with platinum-resistant ovarian cancer who have progressed on standard therapies have few treatment options,” said Dr. Schram. “In this heavily pretreated population, nearly half of patients with platinum-resistant/refractory ovarian cancer responded to rezatapopt, and those responses lasted a median of more than 10 months. These results support rezatapopt as a potential new targeted option for patients whose tumors harbor a TP53 Y220C mutation.”

“The primary analysis reinforces the consistent, durable activity of rezatapopt in patients with platinum-resistant ovarian cancer that has been observed throughout the study,” said Deepika Jalota, Pharm.D., Chief Development Officer of PMV Pharma. “For patients who have endured multiple rounds of chemotherapy, rezatapopt has the potential to be a single-agent, chemotherapy-free, once-daily oral option they can take at home. We expect to submit our NDA for accelerated approval in the first quarter of 2027.”

The Phase 2 clinical trial data as of a September 4, 2026 data cutoff date are summarized below:

Patient Population

  • The safety population consisted of 180 patients across tumor types, including 113 ovarian cancer patients, treated with at least one dose of rezatapopt 2000 mg once daily as monotherapy.
  • The efficacy population consisted of 168 patients, including 101 ovarian cancer patients, treated with at least one dose of rezatapopt as of the data cutoff date and either had ≥1 post-baseline tumor assessment or discontinued early.
  • In the overall population, patients received a median of 3 prior lines of systemic therapy (range: 0-9) and median age was 65 years (range: 33-91).
  • In the ovarian cancer cohort, 93% of patients had high-grade serous ovarian cancer and 97% had platinum-resistant/refractory disease, with a median of 4 prior lines of systemic therapy (range: 1-9).

Efficacy Results

  • Confirmed responses were observed in patients whose tumors were TP53 Y220C mutated and KRAS wild-type in eight tumor types including ovarian, lung, breast, endometrial, head and neck, colorectal, gallbladder cancers, and ampullary carcinoma.
    • In the primary analysis population of platinum-resistant/refractory ovarian cancer patients who had received prior standard of care, the investigator-assessed confirmed overall response rate (ORR) per Response Evaluation Criteria in Solid Tumors (RECIST) v1.1 was 48% (31/65 patients, including one CR and 30 PRs), with a 10.4-month median duration of response and an 83% disease control rate.
      • A biomarker analysis revealed that, among 50 patients with available ctDNA data, 90% (45/50) achieved a ≥50% reduction in ctDNA levels of the TP53 Y220C VAF within 3-6 weeks of starting rezatapopt which supports the on-target activity of rezatapopt.
    • In the ovarian cancer population, responses were observed regardless of additional TP53 alterations or other oncogenic alterations at baseline.
  • In the overall population across all cohorts, a 36% ORR (61/168 patients, including four complete responses [CR], 53 partial responses [PR], and four unconfirmed partial responses [uPR]), with a median time to response of 1.3 months and a median duration of response of 8.1 months was observed.
  • The cohort-specific ORRs were as follows:
    • Ovarian cancer: 45% ORR (45/101 patients, including four confirmed CRs, 37 confirmed PRs, and four uPRs)
    • Lung cancer: 21% confirmed ORR (4/19 patients)
    • Breast cancer: 17% confirmed ORR (3/18 patients)
    • Endometrial cancer: 45% confirmed ORR (5/11 patients)
    • Other solid tumors: 21% confirmed ORR (4/19 patients)

Safety Results

  • Treatment-related adverse events (TRAEs) were mostly Grade 1 or 2 with the most frequent TRAEs observed (>15%) being nausea, fatigue, blood creatinine increase, vomiting, AST increase, ALT increase and anemia. The rates of individual Grade 3 TRAEs were ≤7.2%.
  • Lab abnormalities were manageable and monitorable, with most cases being transient and reversible.
  • Eleven patients (6%), including seven ovarian cancer patients, discontinued treatment due to TRAEs.  
  • Rezatapopt continued to demonstrate a manageable safety profile.

About Rezatapopt

Rezatapopt (PC14586) is a first-in-class, small molecule, p53 reactivator designed to selectively bind to the pocket in the p53 Y220C mutant protein, restoring the wild-type tumor-suppressor function. The U.S. Food and Drug Administration granted Fast Track designation to rezatapopt for the treatment of patients with locally advanced or metastatic solid tumors with a p53 Y220C mutation and Orphan Drug Designation for the treatment of TP53 Y220C positive ovarian cancer, fallopian tube cancer, and primary peritoneal cancer.

About the PYNNACLE Clinical Trial

The ongoing Phase 1/2 PYNNACLE clinical trial is evaluating rezatapopt in patients with advanced solid tumors harboring a TP53 Y220C mutation. The primary objective of the Phase 1 portion of the clinical trial was to determine the maximum tolerated dose and recommended Phase 2 dose (RP2D) of rezatapopt when administered orally to patients. Safety, tolerability, pharmacokinetics, and effects on biomarkers were also assessed. The Phase 2 portion is a registrational, single arm, expansion basket clinical trial comprising five cohorts (ovarian, lung, breast, and endometrial cancers, and other solid tumors) with the primary objective of evaluating the efficacy of rezatapopt at the RP2D in patients with TP53 Y220C advanced solid tumors, conducted across approximately 70 sites.

For more information about the Phase 1/2 PYNNACLE clinical trial, refer to www.clinicaltrials.gov (NCT trial identifier NCT04585750).

About PMV Pharma

PMV Pharma is a precision oncology company pioneering the discovery and development of small molecule therapies targeting p53. TP53 mutations are found in approximately half of all cancers. Our co-founder, Dr. Arnold Levine, established the field of p53 biology when he discovered the p53 protein in 1979. Bringing together leaders in the field to utilize more than four decades of p53 biology, PMV Pharma combines unique biological understanding with a pharmaceutical development focus. PMV Pharma is headquartered in Princeton, New Jersey. For more information, please visit www.pmvpharma.com.

HOUSTON, Nov. 20, 2026 (GLOBE NEWSWIRE) -- Westlake Corporation (NYSE: WLK) today released its 2025 Sustainability Report, marking the company’s ninth annual sustainability report. The report highlights that Westlake has made further progress on its carbon emissions goals. In our 2024 report, Westlake announced that it had achieved its goal of reducing its Scope 1 and Scope 2 CO₂e emissions per ton of production by 20% from a 2016 baseline. In 2025, after reaching the initial target, Westlake committed to a 5% reduction in Scope 1 and 2 CO₂e emissions per ton of production by 2030, using a 2024 baseline.

“At Westlake, we are deeply committed to sustainability and continuous improvement. Achieving our goal of reducing Scope 1 and Scope 2 CO2e emissions per ton of production by 20% from our 2016 baseline early reflects the dedication and innovative spirit of our entire team,” said Jean-Marc Gilson, President and Chief Executive Officer at Westlake Corporation. “But we believe that we should go even further. That is why we decided to commit to a 5% reduction by 2030.”

The report also highlights the completion of a global water risk assessment across 85 sites and that Westlake implemented water reuse projects that save tens of millions of gallons annually. Westlake also notes in its report that in June 2026, it joined the American Chemistry Council to advance safety, sustainability, innovation, and responsible care while strengthening industry leadership and stakeholder dialogue.

“Joining the American Chemistry Council is an important step in strengthening both our competitiveness and our commitment to responsible growth,” said Jean-Marc Gilson, President and CEO of Westlake. “ACC’s Responsible Care program aligns closely with our values and our focus on safety, sustainability and innovation. By working alongside industry peers, we can help ensure that the United States remains a global leader in chemistry, while building more resilient supply chains and delivering the advanced materials that improve everyday life.”

The Sustainability Report features key metrics informed by the Global Reporting Initiative (GRI), Sustainability Accounting Standards Board (SASB), and Task Force on Climate-Related Financial Disclosures (TCFD) frameworks. These internationally recognized standards guide Westlake in providing transparent information about its products, operations, and locations across both the Performance & Essential Materials and Housing & Infrastructure Products businesses.

Celebrating 40 years of operations in 2026, Westlake is a global manufacturer and supplier of materials and innovative products that enhance life every day. PASCAGOULA, Miss.--(BUSINESS WIRE)--Merchants & Marine Bancorp, Inc. (OTCQX: MNMB), the parent company of TownBridge Bank, reported net income available to common shareholders through the third quarter of 2026 of $12.84 million, or $9.13 per share, compared with earnings of $2.30 million, or $1.73 per share, in the same period of the prior year. Gross income through the third quarter totaled $73.34 million, an increase of 82.02% from the prior year. Balance sheet footings increased by 36.95% to $1.30 billion during the 12 months ended September 30, 2026. Net loans grew to $692.90 million over the trailing 12 months from $466.73 million, an increase of 48.46%. Total deposits increased 58.65% during the same period, from $603.81 million at September 30, 2025, to $957.97 million. Significant growth in the balance sheet and in earnings is primarily the result of the successful acquisition of Farmers-Merchants Bank, Breaux Bridge, LA (FM Bank), which closed on April 1, 2026.

Selected financial highlights:

  • Net loans increased to $692.90 million at the end of the third quarter, up from $677.13 million at the end of the second quarter.
  • Total interest income during the third quarter increased to $16.99 million from $12.67 million during the same period in 2025, an increase of 34.11%. Net interest income for the quarter totaled $13.24 million, compared with $9.69 million in the third quarter of 2025.
  • Deposit costs totaled 74 basis points in the third quarter of 2026, essentially unchanged from 73 basis points in the second quarter of 2026.
  • The ratio of loans past due 30-89 days stood at 2.54% of total loans at the end of the third quarter of 2026, an increase from 1.70% at the end of the second quarter. The ratio of non-accrual loans totaled 1.87% of total loans at the end of the third quarter of 2026 compared to 1.94% at the end of the second quarter. The Allowance for Credit Losses (ACL) totaled $7.95 million, or 1.13% of total loans.
  • Accumulated Other Comprehensive Income (AOCI) mark-to-market losses in the securities portfolio totaled ($11.80 million) at the end of the third quarter of 2026, representing 3.05% of the $386.69 million securities portfolio. The increase in AOCI from ($5.81 million) during the second quarter is a result of increases in market rates during the quarter.
  • On-balance sheet liquidity levels remain healthy, with cash and cash equivalents totaling $94.42 million at the end of the third quarter of 2026. In addition to these large cash balances, the Company's investment portfolio remains highly liquid, with a significant portion of the portfolio able to be liquidated with minimal losses.
  • In addition to the sizable on-balance sheet liquidity position, the Company has more than $200 million in additional borrowing capacity at the Federal Home Loan Bank of Dallas and the Federal Reserve.

“We continued a strong earnings trend in the third quarter of 2026, with pre-tax, pre-provision earnings of approximately $2.26 million. This was inclusive of a $158 thousand loss on securities sales as we repositioned the portfolio to better fit the bank after our acquisition of Farmers-Merchants Bank earlier this year,” remarked Casey Hill, the company’s Chief Financial Officer. He continued: “Core earnings continue to accelerate as we realize certain efficiencies after our most recent merger. We do expect these efficiencies to further materialize as we undergo our core and systems conversion in January of 2027. Since the acquisition of FM Bank, we have been operating two core systems along with several other duplicative systems that, once fully merged, are expected to produce significant cost savings.”

“In addition,” continued Hill, “our teams across our Family of Brands continue to perform well. The increase in revenue from our legacy brands, paired with the continued high performance of the FM Bank team bodes well for continued lift in future earnings. While we are experiencing tailwinds in the form of slight elevations in past due loans, we feel confident that the bulk of these should be resolved prior to year-end and are not indicative of broader erosion in our loan portfolio. We are very optimistic about financial performance going forward.”

“Our third quarter results reflect the strong progress our teams are making in bringing FM Bank into our Family of Brands operating model,” remarked Clayton Legear, Chairman & Chief Executive Officer. “Our talented bankers have done an outstanding job of integrating a sizable new brand while continuing to operate our legacy brands at ever stronger levels. We remain encouraged that our operating model allows our brand bankers to serve their clients and communities with the same care and attention they always have and to drive strong results. We are on track for our core systems conversion in January 2027, and we are excited about the enhanced efficiencies and capabilities that will follow.”

Legear continued: “The third quarter also marked an important milestone for our Company. Effective September 28, 2026, our bank charter name officially changed from Merchants & Marine Bank to TownBridge Bank, providing a shared corporate identity for our growing Family of Brands. While our bank charter name has changed, our commitment to our Family of Brands operating model has not. Each of our brands will continue to retain their unique identity, and to be led by local bankers who know their clients, understand their communities, and make decisions close to home. Backed by our Battle-Ready Balance Sheet, our talented team of bankers in every Brand, and the strong momentum building across our Family of Brands, we are better positioned than ever for the future.”

Share Repurchase Program

The share repurchase program authorized by the Board of Directors in the second quarter, covering up to three percent (3%) of the Company's outstanding common stock, remains in effect through June 30, 2027.

Merchants & Marine Bancorp, Inc. (OTCQX: MNMB) is the parent company of TownBridge Bank, a Mississippi chartered community bank serving the Gulf South region. Analysis of credit card transactions finds that sporting goods purchases ramp up earlier than other categories, driven in part by hunting season

MINNEAPOLIS--(BUSINESS WIRE)--

Based on an analysis of credit card transactions processed across a sample of about 50,000 small- and medium-sized retail merchants from 2022 through 2025, Deluxe Corporation (NYSE: DLX) found that while sporting-goods retailers who carry hunting equipment bagged their biggest haul around Thanksgiving, beauty, apparel, and accessory purchases increased sharply in the final two weeks before Christmas.

The boost in sporting goods transactions is likely due to the start of hunting season overlapping with Black Friday in many states, as well as to end-of-year rebates offered by hunting and outdoor adventure equipment manufacturers. In contrast, transactions involving beauty services, apparel, and accessories saw substantially larger increases when Christmas shopping was down to the wire.

These category-specific patterns take on added importance in a year when many consumers are managing tighter budgets. The 2026 Consumer Holiday Spending Study from The Strawhecker Group and the Electronic Transactions Association found that 44% of consumers report greater financial stress than last year and 72% plan to set a holiday budget. With shoppers more deliberate about when and how much they spend, knowing which categories peak early versus late can help retailers make sharper decisions on inventory, staffing, and promotions.

“This is a great example of how the combination of Celero and Deluxe can transform data into useful insights for our customers and partners,” said Kevin Jones, president of Deluxe Merchant Services. “Understanding how and when consumers spend empowers businesses to make better decisions about staffing, inventory, and marketing, and we’re in a great position to help small- and medium-sized businesses interpret the data Deluxe has accumulated.”

Across all retail categories analyzed, the increase in transactions between Thanksgiving week and the mid-December shopping period narrowed substantially over the four-year study. In 2022, average transactions per merchant were 17% higher during the peak Christmas shopping week than during Thanksgiving week. That difference narrowed to 16% in 2023 and just 1% in 2024, before recovering modestly to 4% in 2025.

In 2025:

  • Beauty services: Average transactions per merchant increased 18% in the week before Christmas compared with Thanksgiving week.
  • Apparel and accessories: Average transactions per merchant increased 20% during Christmas week compared with Thanksgiving week.
  • Sporting goods stores processed approximately 18.9% more payment volume per merchant during Thanksgiving week in 2025 than their average weekly volume during the two weeks leading up to Christmas.

The same TSG/ETA study found that 57% of consumers would shop elsewhere or be less likely to return if their preferred payment method wasn’t available—reinforcing that capturing concentrated late-season demand also requires offering the payment options shoppers expect.

Tips to Protect Pipes Before Freezing Temperatures

ALEXANDRIA, Va., Nov. 20, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- As winter approaches, Virginia American Water reminds customers to prepare their home and pipes, providing handy tips to help avoid costly repairs and unwanted stress from frozen pipes. 

"Customers should prepare for frigid temperatures by taking simple steps to protect their pipes from freezing," said Charlie Piekanski, Vice President of Operations, Virginia American Water. "By taking proactive measures, you can help ensure you and your loved ones stay safe and comfortable when the temperature drops."  

You can prepare now by taking the following steps:  

  • Know how to shut off your water: Locate your main water shut-off valve. In many homes, it is located near the water meter or close to where the water pipe enters the home. Hang an I.D. tag on the valve so it can be found quickly during an emergency. Download a tag to print here.
  • Test your main water shut-off valve: Once located, test the shut-off valve by closing it. Once completely closed, check sinks and other water fixtures to ensure the shut-off valve is working properly.  
    • Ball valves generally only require a quarter turn to close. 
    • Gate valves are generally closed by turning the handle clockwise and should turn easily.  
    • If the valve does not close easily, it may need to be serviced.  
    • Bonus: While you are there, check your incoming water service line material! Virginia American Water is working with customers to identify their service line material. If it is found to be made of lead or galvanized steel, they will be replaced in the future. Visit our website for information.  
  • Check sprinkler or irrigation systems: Make sure everything is turned off and fully drained. 
  • Eliminate sources of cold air near water lines: Check for pipes in areas that might be prone to freezing, such as crawl spaces, unheated rooms, basements, garages, and exterior walls. Fix drafty windows, insulate walls around pipes and plug drafts around doors. 
  • Protect your pipes: Where pipes are exposed to cold, wrap them with insulation or heat tape (even fabric or newspaper can help). 

When temperatures stay below freezing: 

  • Give pipes a helping hand: If pipes run through cabinets or vanities, open the doors to let warmer room temperatures flow in. 
  • Keep water moving through the pipes: Allow a small trickle of water to run. The cost of the extra water is typically lower than the cost of repairing a broken pipe. 

If pipes freeze:  

  • Shut off the water immediately: Do not attempt to thaw pipes without turning off the main water shut-off valve. 
  • Thaw a frozen pipe by warming the air around it: Use a hair dryer, space heater or hot water. Do not leave space heaters unattended and avoid using kerosene heaters or open flames.  
  • Once pipes are thawed: Slowly turn the water back on. Check pipes and joints for any cracks or leaks potentially caused by freezing.  

When customers are away from home, consider the following: 

  • Set your thermostat at 55 degrees to prevent freezing. 
  • Have a friend, relative or neighbor regularly check the property to help ensure the heat is working and the pipes have not frozen.  
  • Consider purchasing a freeze alarm. The alarm will call a user-selected phone number if the inside temperature drops below 45 degrees. 

Find cold weather protection tips here: https://amwater.com/corp/Customers-and-Communities/Wise-Water-Use/cold-weather-protection.

Caroline, 9, and Zoe, 12, will appear on limited-edition Well Market snack packaging, and each winner's nonprofit soccer organization will receive a $25,000 grant

WOONSOCKET, R.I., Nov. 20, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- CVS Pharmacy®, the retail division of CVS Health® (NYSE: CVS), and its Well Market® store brand consumables line today named Caroline, age 9, of Holmes Beach, Florida, and Zoe, age 12, of Los Angeles, California, the Grand Prize winners of the first CVS Home Team Heroes soccer contest. The nationwide contest recognizes young soccer players making a meaningful difference in their communities.

Each winner will receive a $25,000 grant for their nonprofit soccer organization, be featured on limited-edition packaging for select Well Market® snacks, CVS Pharmacy's store brand consumables line, and celebrate with a block party for their team. The limited-edition packaging will help bring the winners' stories to a broader audience when it arrives on select CVS Pharmacy shelves in 2027.

"Caroline and Zoe perfectly represent what we set out to celebrate through Home Team Heroes: young players who are showing up for others and making their communities stronger," said Mike Wier, Vice President of Store Brands at CVS Health. "Their stories demonstrate how the values built through soccer can extend far beyond the field. We're proud to recognize their impact, support the soccer organizations they selected to help more young people play, connect and thrive, and share their stories with a broader audience through Well Market."

Jordyn Bugg, Seattle Reign defender, surprised Caroline and Zoe with the news via video.

"Getting to tell Caroline and Zoe they're CVS Home Team Heroes was one of the best moments of my year. I started on a local field with coaches and teammates who believed in me, and it's really special to see these two show up for the players and communities around them," said Bugg. "I can't wait to walk into a CVS and see their faces on the shelf."

Echoing that sentiment, Croix Bethune, Kansas City Current midfielder, celebrated the winners and the impact they're making in their communities.

"Caroline and Zoe show what being a true team player is all about," said Bethune. "I'm honored to be part of sharing their stories and can't wait to see what the future holds for them."

Meet the Home Team Heroes

Caroline, 9, Holmes Beach, Florida
Caroline plays for The Center of Anna Maria Island's youth soccer program in Holmes Beach, Florida. After two hurricanes devastated the Center, Caroline and her older brother, Parker, started Print Wizards, selling 3D-printed toys to raise money for the organization. The siblings have raised more than $6,000 to help repair the fields and establish an all-girls soccer team.

For Caroline, soccer is a place to build camaraderie, confidence and leadership skills alongside her teammates. The Center of Anna Maria Island will use its $25,000 grant to continue rebuilding, support local families affected by the hurricanes and expand youth sports programming so more children can play.  

"As Caroline's parents, we're so proud to see her enthusiasm for her all-girls flag football and soccer team and her business, Print Wizards, recognized through CVS Home Team Heroes," said Brooke and Mike Svoboda. "At nine years old, she's discovering how her ideas can bring people together, and this support means so much to her and our family. It encourages her to keep dreaming big and making a difference in her community."

Zoe, 12, Los Angeles, California
Zoe plays for Tudela Fútbol Club Los Angeles in Los Angeles, California. Born with progressive hearing loss, she serves as a role model for children who are deaf or hard of hearing, regularly meets with newly diagnosed infants and their families, and speaks on student panels to share her experience. Zoe hopes to inspire other deaf soccer players by one day playing for the U.S. Women's Deaf National Team.

Tudela Fútbol Club Los Angeles will use its $25,000 grant to help make soccer more accessible by bridging gender and opportunity gaps and challenging the typical pay-to-play model.

"Discovering the U.S. Women's Deaf National Team gave Zoe something she had been missing: the chance to see herself reflected in the athletes she admired. Through USA Deaf Soccer, she found the confidence to embrace who she is, and when she arrived at her first Tudela FC tryout, someone greeted her in sign language — a simple gesture that showed her she belonged," said Angie Winslow, Zoe's mother. "We're incredibly proud to see Zoe now extending that same spirit of inclusion to younger athletes, and grateful that CVS is celebrating the power of a game that truly belongs to everyone."

What's next for Home Team Heroes
The celebration of this year's Home Team Heroes will continue into 2027. Two Runners-Up will be announced in early 2027, and CVS Pharmacy will visit the Grand Prize winners' hometowns to produce a video series highlighting their stories. The first episode is expected to debut in January. Limited-edition Well Market snacks featuring the winners are anticipated to arrive on CVS Pharmacy shelves in select markets in spring 2027, while supplies last.

Supporting youth soccer in communities
Home Team Heroes builds on CVS Health's broader, multi-year commitment to expanding access to play and supporting healthier communities through soccer. Through community field projects and programs that recognize young athletes making a difference, CVS Health is helping create more opportunities for young people to play.

CVS Health has supported community field projects in collaboration with the Alex Morgan Foundation in Diamond Bar, California, and Secaucus, New Jersey; as well as projects in Vancouver, Washington; Kansas City, Missouri; and Garfield Park in Washington, D.C.

FORT WORTH, Texas, Nov. 20, 2026 (GLOBE NEWSWIRE) -- Sports Entertainment Gaming Global Corporation ("SEGG Media" or the "Company") (Nasdaq: SEGG) today announced that TicketStub.com will relaunch on a new platform on November 25, at the start of the holiday shopping season. TicketStub.com will open with a Black Friday offer, with details to be announced closer to launch, and will release promo codes for discounted tickets throughout the holidays.

Half of U.S. holiday shoppers plan to give an experience this year, up from 39% in 2024, and 19% plan to give tickets to an event, according to Deloitte's 2026 Holiday Retail Survey. The same survey found that 47% of shoppers would rather give one meaningful, higher-cost gift than several smaller ones. On the receiving side, concert tickets ranked second only to a full trip among the experiences Americans most wanted as a holiday gift, cited by 51% of respondents in a 2025 Talker Research survey of 5,000 adults commissioned by Chime.

Demand for live events is running at record levels. Live Nation Entertainment reported selling 170 million concert tickets through October 2026, up 13% year over year and already ahead of its total for all of 2025.

TicketStub.com gives users access to thousands of events around the world and earns revenue through service fees. The Company plans to add advertising and promoted listings as the platform develops. The relaunch follows the worldwide relaunch of Lottery.com on November 18 and is supported by the strategic financing commitments SEGG Media announced on November 12.

"Veloce's channels draw more than 500 million views a month from fans who follow racing, gaming and live sport. That's an audience that goes to live events, and putting TicketStub.com in front of them is our first priority," said Gregory Potts, Chief Operating Officer of SEGG Media. "We also plan to add an ongoing sweepstakes where users can win free tickets, concert experiences and other live event prizes. Two businesses
Caliber is one public company with two businesses. Its real estate investment platform has sponsored, built and managed middle-market real estate since 2009 and produces substantially all of Caliber's revenue today. It is the foundation of the Company, and its objective is steady, consistent profitability. Its tokenization platform, built around Caliber Tokenization Services, brings tokenization to private real estate funds, starting with the funds Caliber manages, and is designed to be Caliber's growth engine. Caliber holds LINK, the token of the Chainlink network, in its corporate treasury as part of its tokenization strategy; today it is not a pure play LINK treasury company.

VANCOUVER, Wash.--(BUSINESS WIRE)-- ZoomInfo (NASDAQ: GTM), the all-in-one AI GTM platform, today announced that Qualified from Salesforce has upgraded its ZoomInfo integration to the ZoomInfo GTM.AI API. Qualified now enriches website visitor profiles through the API's company and contact enrichment endpoints, replacing the legacy WebSights and Enterprise APIs, so Piper, Qualified's agent, works from verified ZoomInfo company and contact data.

For Qualified customers, the integration works as it did before. They connect their ZoomInfo account in Qualified, and visitor profiles are enriched automatically, with no change to their setup.

The integration enriches each website visitor at two points. When a visitor arrives on a customer's website, Qualified uses reverse IP enrichment to add ZoomInfo company data to the visitor's profile. When a visitor shares an email address, Qualified uses email enrichment to add ZoomInfo contact data.

Both enrichment steps run automatically, at the same two points every time. The data flows into Qualified visitor fields, the context Qualified holds on each website visitor. Customers choose which fields Piper can use in conversations and which fields drive deterministic workflows such as segmentation and routing.

The API gives partners and customers programmatic access to ZoomInfo's verified company and contact data. The Qualified integration uses two of its endpoints, company enrichment and contact enrichment, and only the fields those endpoints return.

Customers connect the integration with their existing ZoomInfo account.

“Qualified customers already generate pipeline with Piper,” said Dennis Sevilla, Chief Strategy Officer at ZoomInfo. “ZoomInfo adds verified company and contact data to every visitor profile. Piper starts each conversation knowing more about who she is talking to, and teams can segment and route visitors on data they trust.”

Qualified customers can connect ZoomInfo from the Qualified settings page at app.qualified.com/settings/zoominfo. Customers who do not see the option can contact their Qualified Success Architect (QSA). Details are also available on the ZoomInfo integrations page at zoominfo.com/integrations/qualified.

The upgrade puts Qualified on the same GTM.AI API that ZoomInfo partners use to bring verified company and contact data into their platforms.

About ZoomInfo

ZoomInfo (NASDAQ: GTM), the all-in-one AI GTM platform, enables sales, marketing, and customer success teams to execute their go-to-market strategy with confidence. Powered by the industry's most comprehensive B2B data, including more than 100 million companies, 500 million contacts, and billions of signals, ZoomInfo delivers the intelligence, automation, and integrations that modern revenue teams need to identify, engage, and convert their best buyers.

GTM.AI is a headless layer that connects to ZoomInfo's GTM Context Graph. It is the API and Model Context Protocol home for AI agents, powering integrations across Salesforce, HubSpot, Microsoft, Anthropic, OpenAI, Perplexity, and dozens more.

Key Terms

apitechnical
An API, or Application Programming Interface, is a set of rules that allows different software programs to communicate and work together smoothly, much like a waiter translating your order into the kitchen and then bringing your meal back. For investors, APIs are important because they enable real-time access to financial data, trading systems, and other digital services, making it easier to make informed decisions quickly and efficiently.
model context protocoltechnical
A model context protocol is a set of rules or guidelines that determine how a financial model interprets and applies information within a specific situation. It helps ensure consistent and accurate analysis by clarifying what data or assumptions are relevant in a given scenario. For investors, it provides clarity on how predictions or assessments are made, increasing confidence in decision-making.
